source: BHPS Class VI French midterm model paper 2026-27 + teaching notes, Chapter 1

overview.bigIdea: A French verb changes its ending to match the person. **Find the subject → pick the right ending.** Learn two regular patterns (-ER, -IR) and eight irregular verbs from the model paper.
overview.languagesTitle: Three things to be able to do

languages.name: Say
languages.text: Say each table aloud in 10 seconds.

languages.name: Choose
languages.text: Pick the right form for any subject.

languages.name: Spot
languages.text: Find the mistake in a sentence.

plan.text: Read the four lessons, say tables aloud.

lessons.title: Verbes en -ER
lessons.hook: Most French verbs end in **-er**: parler, aimer, habiter, regarder. Good news – they all follow **one pattern**.

core.def: Remove -er, add: je -e · tu -es · il/elle -e · nous -ons · vous -ez · ils/elles -ent
je parle, tu parles, il parle, nous parlons, vous parlez, ils parlent
Before a vowel or h: j’aime, j’habite, j’écoute.
nous mangeons (keep the e so the g stays soft).

explain: -e, -es, -e and -ent all sound the same – only spelling changes.
Always find the subject first; ‘Le garçon’ = il, ‘Mes amis’ = ils.
mistakes: Forgetting j’ before a vowel (je aime ✗).
lessons.tip: Underline the subject before you write the verb.
lessons.memory: E-ES-E, ONS-EZ-ENT – say it like a chant!
examAsk: Conjugate an -ER verb for a given subject.
Correct the verb in a sentence.

play.title: parler table
play.say: Match each subject with the right form of parler.

lessons.title: Verbes en -IR (finir)
lessons.hook: Le garçon **finit** le travail. Regular **-IR** verbs have a secret: **-iss-** in the plural!

core.def: je finis, tu finis, il finit, nous finissons, vous finissez, ils finissent

explain: The -iss- appears only with nous, vous, ils/elles.
Teaching note: finir, choisir, grandir, réussir are regular -IR verbs.
lessons.tip: When you see nous/vous/ils with an -IR verb, check for -iss-.
examAsk: Model paper Q6(b): Le garçon ___ le travail. (finir) → finit.

play.title: finir table
play.say: Match each subject with the right form of finir.

lessons.title: être, avoir, aller, faire
lessons.hook: The four most-used verbs are **irregular** – no pattern, just learn them. They appear everywhere!

core.def: suis, es, est, sommes, êtes, sont
ai, as, a, avons, avez, ont
vais, vas, va, allons, allez, vont
fais, fais, fait, faisons, faites, font

explain: être = to be (Je suis en sixième); avoir = to have (J’ai un chien); aller = to go (Nous allons au restaurant); faire = to do (Je fais du vélo).
Q1(d) of the paper asks the infinitive: sommes → être, ai → avoir.
lessons.tip: Group the -ont forms: ils sont, ils ont, ils vont, ils font.
examAsk: Give the infinitive of a form (sommes, ai).

play.title: aller table
play.say: Match each subject with the right form of aller.

play.title: Which verb?
play.say: Which infinitive does each form come from?

lessons.title: lire, prendre, comprendre, mettre
lessons.hook: Model paper Q6: Elle **lit** le roman · Tu ne **comprends** pas la leçon ? · Ils **mettent** les livres sur la table.

core.def: lis, lis, lit, lisons, lisez, lisent
prends, prends, prend, prenons, prenez, prennent
mets, mets, met, mettons, mettez, mettent

explain: prendre and comprendre: il prend (no t!), ils prennent (double n).
mettre: il met (one t), nous mettons (two t).

example.q: Conjugate: Ils ___ les livres sur la table. (mettre)
example.answer: Ils mettent les livres sur la table.

lessons.memory: prennent needs two n’s, like ‘penne’ pasta!
examAsk: Model paper Q6: lire, comprendre, mettre.

play.title: prendre table
play.say: Match each subject with the right form of prendre.

revision: Find the **subject** first: Le garçon = il, Mes amis = ils.
Irregular: **être, avoir, aller, faire, lire, prendre, mettre** – learn the tables.
je → **j’** before a vowel: j’ai, j’aime.

paper.what: Conjugate: lire, finir, comprendre, aller, mettre

sections.title: How to conjugate in the exam
items: Write the stem + ending (or the learnt form).

sections.title: Writing answers that score
items: Copy the spelling carefully – accents count (é, è, ê, ç).
Always start a sentence with a capital letter and end with a full stop or question mark.
Before writing a verb, find the subject first (je, tu, il, nous…) and use the matching ending.
For negation, check two things: ne…pas around the verb, and un/une/des → de after pas.
In descriptions write 5 simple sentences: name → where → what you see or do → why you like it → a feeling.
Answer culture questions in a full sentence: ‘La capitale de la France est Paris.’

sections.title: The day before the test
items: Say each verb table aloud once (je, tu, il, nous, vous, ils).
Redo the Play & learn activities – aim for every card right first time.
Take one Check knowledge quiz at Hard level.

checklist: I can conjugate -ER verbs for all subjects.
I can conjugate finir and other -IR verbs.
I know être, avoir, aller, faire by heart.
I know lire, prendre, comprendre, mettre.
I can give the infinitive of a verb form.
exam.paperTitle: In the Class VI midterm model paper
exam.paperNote: BHPS Class VI French midterm model paper 2026-27 (80 marks: Reading 10 · Writing 20 · Grammar 30 · Culture 20). Practise these question types first.

method: Built on how languages stick: hear and see short patterns, practise them many times with instant feedback, say answers aloud before checking (active recall), and revisit after 1, 3 and 7 days (spaced revision).
